item.title: PHP developers say key patches available after global scare
item.description: Newly discovered vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language have put millions of websites at risk, with government agencies across the world sounding alarm bells. PHP developers are now urging immediate updates.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
item.description: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
item.description: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany news: Nvidia CEO optimistic about EU's AI economy
item.description: Jensen Huang, the head of the chip giant, was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. Meanwhile, a cigarette tax hike came into effect early due to a "technical error." DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Pakistan-Taliban conflict: How India could benefit from shifting regional dynamics
item.description: As Pakistan's influence in Afghanistan comes under strain, India is rebuilding ties with the Taliban in Kabul. Can New Delhi turn this diplomatic opening into lasting strategic gains?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: UK approves Jackdaw gas field after years in limbo
item.description: Drilling is set to begin in the controversial North Sea plot as the government seeks to tackle high energy costs. Environmental groups have criticized the move and called for more clean energy.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
item.description: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs after car attack as suspect appears in court
item.description: Doctors have amputated both of Helen Haines legs after the Australian lawmaker was hit in an apparent deliberate attack. The suspected driver involved in the attack has appeared in court.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
item.description: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: India news: India-US trade deal 'pretty close,' says Trump
item.description: US President Donald Trump hinted that the US-India trade deal could look different from the previous ones.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger 'good idea' as companies explore union
item.description: Musk confirmed the long standing speculation of a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX but warned that it would be premature to assume it is happening for sure.

item.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
item.description: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

item.title: Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink in Ukraine — report
item.description: Elon Musk "capped the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network," the Wall Street Journal reported.

item.title: UK fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: The UK is sending military support to Saudi Arabia as Iran-aligned Houthi rebels launch repeated attacks on the kingdom.

item.title: Portugal housing protests continue after police clear camps
item.description: Demonstrators vow to continue their campaign to call for affordable housing in Portugal after police cleared tent camps and arrested at least 55 people.

item.title: AfD's Alice Weidel to unveil plan to cut EU powers — report
item.description: The far-right AfD will propose slashing powers of the European Union when it presents its policy paper on Wednesday, Politico reports.

item.title: Zelenskyy visits Norway amid Trump White House tensions
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy met with Norwegian and Finnish leaders in Oslo and held talks with Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Trump is pressuring Zelenskyy to "make a deal" with Russia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Nigeria records its first Ebola case, in capital Abuja
item.description: Nigeria has reported its first known case of Ebola during Africa's latest outbreak originating in the DRC. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the patient was a woman who had recently flown to Abuja from Uganda.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Lebanon faces uncertainty as UNIFIL mandate nears end
item.description: As UN peacekeeping forces prepare to withdraw from Lebanon, Israel remains present and Hezbollah is still armed. A new EU support mission aims to strengthen Lebanon's army, but will not replace UN peacekeepers.

item.title: New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
item.description: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
item.description: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
item.description: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
item.description: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

item.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
item.description: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

item.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
item.description: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
item.description: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
item.description: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

item.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?

item.title: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?

item.title: Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
item.description: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

item.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
item.description: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

item.title: Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

item.title: France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
item.description: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

item.description: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

item.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?

item.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?

item.title: Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama

item.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter

item.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

item.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget

item.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
item.description: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
item.description: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
item.description: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
item.description: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
item.description: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
item.description: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Spain grows fruit and vegetables for Europe, but it's running out of water
item.description: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
item.description: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
item.description: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
item.description: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
item.description: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
item.description: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
item.description: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
item.description: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
item.description: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
item.description: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
item.description: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
item.description: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
item.description: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
item.description: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
item.description: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
item.description: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?
item.dc:subject: Business
